summary: Researched current US retail prices (session date 2026-08-13) for golf-sim projectors, computers, and cabling/mounting gear. Key finding: the sub-$700 short-throw "golf-sim-grade" projector tier the brief assumed has effectively disappeared — Optoma's GT1080HDR/GT1080HDRx (the class example) were discontinued in 2023, and current dedicated golf-sim short-throw units (BenQ TH671ST, Optoma ZW350ST) now start around $909-950. A true sub-$700 option exists only if you drop the short-throw requirement (Optoma HD146X, standard throw, $599.99). Mid and high-end projector tiers are well populated and verified directly against a golf-sim retailer's live collection page. Computer prices for RTX 4060/4070 gaming laptops are confirmed via multiple converging retailer sources but several are deal-priced and can shift; refurb budget-laptop pricing could not be pinned to a single live page this session (site blocked direct fetch) so it's flagged unverified. Cabling/mounting prices are solid except the cable ramp, which is flagged unverified for the same reason (403 on direct fetch).

findings.product: Optoma HD146X (1080p, 3600 lumens, STANDARD throw ~1.5:1 — not short throw)
findings.notes: Only projector found in the $400-700 band. Not short-throw, so it needs real distance behind the hitting mat to fill a 13x10ft screen — workable in a garage bay or basement with depth, not in a tight enclosure footprint. The GT1080HDR/GT1080HDRx class the brief named as the budget benchmark was discontinued by Optoma in 2023 and is no longer sold new; secondary-market/open-box units were not reliably priced this session.

findings.product: BenQ TH671ST (1080p, 3000 lumens, short throw 0.69-0.83:1) — closest short-throw option to budget
findings.notes: Priced consistently at $949 across three retailers checked this session (Best Buy $949.99, topshelfgolf.com $949, indoorgolfoutlet.com $949, marked down from $1,189 list). Marketed explicitly as BenQ's entry-level golf-sim projector, but ~$250-350 above the brief's $400-700 budget band — flagging this gap honestly rather than forcing a fit.
findings.tier_fit: budget-to-mid boundary; effectively today's cheapest true short-throw golf-sim projector

findings.product: Optoma ZW350ST (WXGA 1024x768 native/enhanced, 3600 lumens, laser, short throw 0.496:1)
findings.notes: Verified via direct fetch of a golf-sim retailer's live projector catalog this session. Sub-1080p native resolution (upscales), IP6X dust rated, 30,000hr laser light source — good fit for a frequently-transported rig since there's no lamp to break.

findings.product: Optoma GT2000HDR (1080p, 3500 lumens, laser, short throw 0.496:1, HDR10)
findings.notes: Verified via direct fetch same session/source. True 1080p, laser light source, good lumens for variable ambient light in an inflatable enclosure.
Verified via direct fetch same session/source. Newer than GT2000HDR in the same product family.

findings.product: Optoma ZK431ST-B (4K UHD, short throw, laser)
findings.notes: Verified via direct fetch this session. True 4K UHD input at the low end of the high-end band.
Verified via direct fetch this session, from the same golf-sim-specific retailer catalog.
Verified via direct fetch this session. Top of the requested high-end band.

findings.product: BenQ LK936ST (4K, 5100 ANSI lumens, laser, 0.81-0.89:1 short throw) — the "golf sim standard" the brief named
findings.notes: Confirmed at the identical $4,899 price on two independent golf-sim retailers this session (topshelfgolf.com and shopindoorgolf.com's catalog), down from $5,849 MSRP. This is the industry-recognized golf-sim benchmark unit but it runs well above the $1500-3000 high-end band specified — flagging the mismatch rather than mislabeling it.

findings.product: Refurbished Acer Nitro V (Ryzen 7 7735HS or similar, RTX 4060, 16GB RAM) via Target/eBay refurb channel
findings.notes: UNVERIFIED as a live price this session — Target's specific refurb listing 404'd on direct fetch and the $549.99-$624.99 figures I found trace to Jan/Feb 2025 deal articles (PCWorld), so they are stale, not current-session prices. Refurb gaming-laptop inventory turns over fast; treat $600-750 as a directional budget-tier estimate only, and check the live Target/eBay/Amazon Renewed listing before quoting a number in the plan.

findings.product: RTX 4060 gaming laptop, new (MSI Cyborg 15 / Acer Nitro V class, 16GB RAM, RTX 4060)
findings.notes: Direct page fetch timed out (Best Buy blocks the fetch tool), but the $899-999 figure is corroborated across multiple independent sources found this session (Laptop Mag, PCWorld, Best Buy listing title/SKU). List price is typically $1,099; this class sits on/near sale pricing often. GSPro's own stated minimum for 1080p is an RTX 3060 w/16GB RAM, so an RTX 4060 laptop comfortably clears the bar with headroom for 1080p Ultra.

findings.product: Lenovo Legion Slim 5 Gen 9 (AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS, RTX 4070, 16GB RAM, 16in WQXGA 165Hz)
findings.notes: Direct fetch to the specific Lenovo product page returned 403 (bot-blocked); price sourced from a Laptop Mag deals roundup this session citing Lenovo.com directly, $538 off a $1,769 list. Deal pricing can expire — verify current price at the Lenovo RTX 4070 laptop category link before committing.

findings.product: ASUS ROG Zephyrus G16 (Intel Core Ultra 9, RTX 4070, 16GB RAM, 16in OLED 240Hz)
findings.notes: Sourced from a Laptop Mag deals roundup this session ($525 off $1,999 list at Best Buy); direct Best Buy product fetch timed out. Premium OLED panel makes this a strong high-end pick if display quality matters as much as the GSPro frame rate.
findings.tier_fit: high-end laptop, RTX 4070 class, premium display

findings.product: ASUS ROG NUC mini PC (Core Ultra 9 185H, RTX 4070 laptop GPU, 8GB GDDR6)
findings.notes: Mini-PC path the brief asked about as an alternative to a laptop. Price and existence confirmed via search this session on notebookcheck.net; not independently page-verified by direct fetch. Sits at the top of a reasonable high-end budget — a mini PC skips the built-in display/battery/keyboard cost of a laptop but needs its own monitor for setup/diagnostics away from the projector.

findings.product: Tripp Lite P568-050-BK-GRP High-Speed HDMI Cable, 50ft, gripping connectors
findings.notes: Verified via direct page fetch this session (Newegg, seller TELeasy). Other marketplace sellers on the same listing ranged $56.99-$60.13. A reputable, known-durable brand for a cable that gets coiled/uncoiled repeatedly during transport.

findings.product: J-Tech Digital Wireless HDMI Extender Kit, 1080p 60Hz, 200ft range (JTECH-WEX200V3)
findings.notes: Verified via direct fetch of the manufacturer's own product page this session. Avoids running a 50ft HDMI cable across the enclosure floor every setup, at the cost of needing two more devices to pack/transport.
findings.tier_fit: cabling/misc, transport-convenience upgrade over a physical cable

findings.product: APC SurgeArrest Essential PE625 — 6-outlet surge protector, 25ft cord, 1080 Joules
findings.notes: Price confirmed identically across two independent searches this session referencing the same Home Depot listing; direct page fetch was blocked (403) so this is search-tool-verified rather than raw-HTML-verified. 25ft cord is useful for a mobile rig where the nearest outlet position varies by venue.
findings.tier_fit: cabling/misc — power protection for projector + PC

findings.product: Pyle Cable Ramp Protective Cover (2-channel, drop-over, ~2000lbs capacity) — representative cable ramp option
findings.notes: UNVERIFIED — direct page fetch returned 403 on both Home Depot and B&H Photo this session, and search snippets showed inconsistent figures ($55.03 on one Home Depot listing page vs. $24-$39.99 for a different VEVOR 4-pack SKU with store-card discounts baked in). Budget $25-55 for a cable ramp depending on channel count and brand; confirm the exact SKU price live before including it in a budget line.
